analysis.evidence: הַפָּלִיט names the one who came. The next clause, וַיַּגֵּד לְאַבְרָם, recounts what the fugitive did upon arrival: he told Abram.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, agreeing with הַפָּלִיט, “the fugitive.”

analysis.evidence: The same man is the subject of וַיָּבֹא (“he came”) and וַיַּגֵּד (“he told”). The narrator identifies him by his escape as he brings news to Abram.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: The escapee is the subject of both וַיָּבֹא (“he came”) and וַיַּגֵּד (“he told”). The following לְאַבְרָם identifies Abram as the recipient of the news.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, agreeing with הַפָּלִיט, the escapee.
analysis.sense: tell someone that something is the case

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּגֵּד לְאַבְרָם הָעִבְרִי, the fugitive reports to Abram, whom the verse identifies as “the Hebrew.”
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ marks Abram, a masculine personal name, as the recipient of the report.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: In לְאַבְרָם הָעִבְרִי, the fugitive reports to “Abram the Hebrew.” The parallel phrase מַמְרֵא הָאֱמֹרִי, “Mamre the Amorite,” likewise identifies a named man by his people.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes a masculine singular absolute gentilic used in apposition to Abram.

analysis.evidence: הוּא refers back to אַבְרָם הָעִבְרִי and serves as the subject of שֹׁכֵן, “dwelling.” The clause tells where Abram was living when the fugitive brought him the news.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ introduces a background clause. הוּא is an independent third-person masculine singular pronoun.

analysis.evidence: The pronoun הוּא refers to Abram, and בְּאֵלֹנֵי מַמְרֵא identifies where he was living when the fugitive brought him the news.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, used predicatively with הוּא to describe Abram’s ongoing residence.
analysis.sense: dwell or live in a place

analysis.evidence: שֹׁכֵן בְּאֵלֹנֵי מַמְרֵא locates Abram’s dwelling by the terebinths of Mamre. The trees identify the place where he was living.
analysis.morphology: The locative preposition בְּ precedes אֵלֹנֵי, the masculine plural construct of אֵלוֹן. The following name מַמְרֵא completes the construct phrase.
analysis.sense: A great tree or terebinth serving as a landmark.

evidence.note: The verse calls Mamre הָאֱמֹרִי, “the Amorite,” names Eshcol and Aner as his brothers, and describes them as Abram’s covenant allies.

article.name: מַמְרֵא
article.summary: Mamre is an Amorite, brother of Eshcol and Aner. Abram camps among his terebinths. The derivation of his name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for the man identified in Genesis 14:13. The existing place-name sense covers the locality at Hebron in Genesis 13:18.
draft.definition: Mamre, the Amorite brother of Eshcol and Aner.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:13 names Mamre, gives his kinship to Eshcol and Aner, and identifies the men as Abram’s covenant allies.

analysis.evidence: הָאֱמֹרִי identifies Mamre as “the Amorite,” and אֲחִי אֶשְׁכֹּל וַאֲחִי עָנֵר calls him “brother of Eshcol and brother of Aner.” These descriptions identify the person whose terebinths are mentioned.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. It completes the construct phrase בְּאֵלֹנֵי מַמְרֵא, “among the terebinths of Mamre.”
analysis.sense: Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eshcol and Aner and an ally of Abram.

draft.change: Associate this occurrence with the existing noun אֱמֹרִי at word index 0 and its sense amorite. The article already cites this verse.
draft.definition: A member of the Amorite people, or collectively the people as a whole.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:13 calls Mamre הָאֱמֹרִי, an individual use of the gentilic.

analysis.evidence: In מַמְרֵא הָאֱמֹרִי, the gentilic identifies Mamre by his people. The following words call him the brother of Eshcol and Aner, confirming that the designation applies to one man.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ־ prefixes a masculine singular gentilic noun in the absolute state.
analysis.sense: An individual member of the Amorite people.

analysis.evidence: אֲחִי אֶשְׁכֹּל identifies Mamre the Amorite as Eshcol’s brother. The parallel phrase וַאֲחִי עָנֵר identifies Aner as another brother of Mamre.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state. The following name אֶשְׁכֹּל completes the construct phrase.

evidence.note: Mamre is called “brother of Eshcol and brother of Aner.” The men are identified as Abram’s covenant partners.
Abram names Aner, Eshcol and Mamre as the men who went with him.
The verse explains the place name Valley of Eshcol by the cluster of grapes cut there, illustrating the meaning of the matching common noun.

article.name: אֶשְׁכֹּל
article.summary: Eshcol is Mamre’s brother and one of Abram’s allies. His name has the same form as the Hebrew noun for a cluster of grapes. Genesis gives no explanation for his personal name.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article. The source gloss “young camel” has no support in the verse, and the source root אשה has no established connection to the name.
draft.definition: Eshcol, brother of Mamre and ally of Abram.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:13 identifies Eshcol by kinship with Mamre. Genesis 14:24 names Aner, Eshcol and Mamre together as the men who went with Abram.

analysis.evidence: The parallel phrases אֲחִי אֶשְׁכֹּל וַאֲחִי עָנֵר identify Mamre as the brother of both Eshcol and Aner. The following וְהֵם בַּעֲלֵי בְרִית אַבְרָם identifies the men as Abram’s covenant partners.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun naming a man, with no prefix or suffix. It completes the construct phrase אֲחִי אֶשְׁכֹּל, “brother of Eshcol.”
analysis.sense: Eshcol, Mamre’s brother and Abram’s ally

analysis.evidence: The parallel phrases אֲחִי אֶשְׁכֹּל וַאֲחִי עָנֵר identify Mamre as the brother of both Eshcol and Aner. The following clause separately describes their covenant with Abram.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ־ means “and.” אֲחִי is the masculine singular construct of אָח, with עָנֵר as its complement.

evidence.note: וַאֲחִי עָנֵר identifies Aner as Mamre’s brother, and בַּעֲלֵי בְרִית אַבְרָם identifies the men as Abram’s covenant partners.

article.name: עָנֵר
article.summary: Mamre is called the brother of Eshcol and Aner. The three men are covenant partners of Abram. The meaning of Aner’s name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for עָנֵר. Leave its root unassigned because the derivation is uncertain.
draft.definition: Aner, brother of Mamre and covenant partner of Abram.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:13 identifies Aner through his kinship with Mamre and his covenant with Abram.

analysis.evidence: The parallel phrases אֲחִי אֶשְׁכֹּל and וַאֲחִי עָנֵר identify Mamre as brother of both Eshcol and Aner. The closing clause calls the men Abram’s covenant partners. The name ends in ר, and the verse gives no basis for the proposed root ענק or the description “son of Benjamin.”
analysis.morphology: An unprefixed masculine personal name, singular in reference, with no suffix. It completes the construct phrase וַאֲחִי עָנֵר, “and brother of Aner.”
analysis.sense: Aner, brother of Mamre and ally of Abram

draft.change: Add Gen.14.13 as evidence for the existing sense they under הֵם in hw2.
draft.definition: The independent masculine plural subject pronoun refers back to people or things already mentioned.
draft.evidence: In Gen.14.13 הֵם takes up the three men named immediately before it as the subject of בַּעֲלֵי בְרִית אַבְרָם.

analysis.evidence: After naming Mamre and his brothers Eshcol and Aner, the verse says וְהֵם בַּעֲלֵי בְרִית אַבְרָם, “and they were Abram’s allies.” הֵם supplies the subject, and the plural בַּעֲלֵי begins the predicate.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ joins the clause to the preceding description. הֵם is the independent third-person masculine plural personal pronoun and serves as the subject.
analysis.sense: they, referring to Mamre, Eshcol, and Aner

analysis.evidence: The plural וְהֵם refers to Mamre, Eshcol, and Aner. The phrase בַּעֲלֵי בְרִית אַבְרָם identifies the three as Abram’s allies by virtue of their covenant with him.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural construct noun. Its complement is בְרִית.

analysis.evidence: The phrase בַּעֲלֵי בְרִית אַבְרָם identifies Mamre, Eshcol, and Aner as parties to a covenant with Abram, hence as his allies.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the construct state, followed by אַבְרָם. The initial ב belongs to the noun.
analysis.sense: covenant between men: treaty, alliance, pact

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.

draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: The fugitive brings word to Abram earlier in the verse. The closing phrase בַּעֲלֵי בְרִית אַבְרָם identifies Mamre, Eshcol, and Aner as Abram’s allies.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun without a prefix or suffix. It stands at the end of the construct chain בַּעֲלֵי בְרִית אַבְרָם.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham
